claim: Layers a second feeling underneath the primary one, because real performance is almost never a single clean emotion — the mix is the acting. A director sets it when the line is 'happy for her, and hollow about it' and one emotion word flattens the face.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

review.issue: The option list is not an enum. "plus any char.emotion value" is a meta-description, not a value, so the card cannot produce one panel per option — it produces two panels, one empty and one hardcoded example. The single clause "smiling, teary eyes, furrowed brow" also carries the PRIMARY emotion (smiling) inside a clause that is supposed to express only the secondary layer.
review.fix: Hold one primary fixed and enumerate real secondary values against it, one panel each. e.g. primary is always "smile" in the subject-adjacent slot, then options: none ("smile"), grief ("smile, teary eyes"), anger ("smile, furrowed brow, tense jaw"), fear ("smile, wide eyes, sweatdrop"), exhaustion ("smile, half-closed eyes, eye bags"), contempt ("smile, half-lidded eyes, one raised eyebrow"). If the schema really is a free cross-product, the card should say so and render 4-6 representative pairs as the demonstration set.
